examples.title: Factorial: recursion
examples.description: Recursive 4! = 24. The call stack grows to five frames (main plus four calls) and unwinds again, multiplying results on the way back, which shows how the JVM resumes a method exactly where it left off.

examples.title: Fibonacci: branching recursion
examples.tagline: Every call splits in two: fib(7) = 13.
examples.description: Naive fib(7) = 13. Every call branches into two more, so the stack grows and unwinds dozens of times. The cost of naive recursion is visible: the same subproblems are recomputed from scratch again and again.

examples.title: Sum of products: nested for loops
examples.tagline: Flat stack, long run: Σ i·j over a 6×6 grid.
examples.description: Sum of i*j over a 6x6 grid. A flat call stack but hundreds of steps, covering iinc (incrementing a counter in place, without touching the operand stack), the if_icmpgt condition and the backward goto.

examples.title: GCD: while loop and remainder
examples.description: Euclid's algorithm for (1071, 462) = 21. The loop condition compiles to ifne on the remainder from irem, and the body copies values between local variable slots.

examples.title: Bubble sort: arrays on the heap
examples.tagline: An array on the heap: {5,3,4,1,2} sorted in place.
examples.description: Bubble sort over {5, 3, 4, 1, 2}. The one example with an array: newarray allocates it, iastore fills it and iaload reads back the two neighbours every comparison needs. Each swap rewrites the heap, and result ends up holding a[0] = 1, the minimum the sort moved to the front.

examples.title: Collatz: printing as it runs
examples.tagline: One console line per step: 7 falls to 1.
examples.description: The Collatz sequence from 7, printed term by term. Halve an even number, triple an odd one and add one: sixteen steps later it reaches 1. The only example that prints, so the console grows by a line per iteration; getstatic reads System.out and invokevirtual hands it the number.

examples.title: Days in a year: switch dispatch
examples.tagline: One jump table, twelve months, 365 days.
examples.description: The length of a common year, month by month. Dense case labels make javac emit tableswitch: ten table entries for five cases, so the four thirty-day months share a target and the months missing from the table fall to the default one. Every call reaches its arm in the same number of steps, whatever the month.

examples.title: Fast power: shifts and masks
examples.tagline: Reading 13 bit by bit: 3^13 in four steps.
examples.description: Exponentiation by squaring, 3^13 = 1594323. The bits of the exponent drive the loop: iand against a mask of one asks whether the lowest bit is set, iushr throws it away and brings down the next. Four iterations instead of thirteen multiplications, with the operand stack doing the work.
